STYLE OF CAUSE: Patel v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
CITATION: 2020 FC 331
COURT: Federal Court
DOCKET: IMM-4455-19
DATE: 2020-03-02

FACTS
[1] The applicant sought judicial review of a decision refusing his application for permanent residence.
[2] The visa officer found the applicant had not established sufficient settlement funds.

ANALYSIS
[3] The officer's reasons do not engage meaningfully with the evidence of the applicant's job offer in Canada.
[4] This omission renders the decision unreasonable.

DISPOSITION
[5] The application for judicial review is granted and the matter is remitted for redetermination by a different officer.

STYLE OF CAUSE: Wong v. British Columbia (Workers' Compensation Appeal Tribunal)
CITATION: 2019 BCCA 287
COURT: Court of Appeal for British Columbia
DOCKET: CA45678
DATE: 2019-08-19

I. BACKGROUND
[1] The petitioner appeals a decision of the Workers' Compensation Appeal Tribunal denying her claim for a chronic pain disorder.

II. ANALYSIS
[2] The Tribunal's conclusion that the medical evidence was insufficient was reasonably open to it on the record.
[3] There is no basis to interfere with the Tribunal's weighing of the competing medical opinions.

III. DISPOSITION
[4] The appeal is dismissed.
